label: Brand Chip
title: Brand Chip
summary: Use Brand Chip to identify a linked brand or account with an avatar and a short label.
corePrinciple: Pair a recognizable identity with just enough text to distinguish it.

anatomy.title: Identity and identifier
anatomy.description: A small avatar and short label form one recognizable account identifier.
blocks: Names the account and distinguishes it from similar accounts.

anatomy.note: Names the account and distinguishes it from similar accounts.

configuration.title: Choose a recognizable identity
configuration.description: Keep the avatar and label about the same brand. A monogram can provide a clear fallback when an image is unavailable.

states.title: Read-only or actionable
states.description: Use a static chip to identify the current account. Make it actionable only when it opens account detail or a choice.

sizing.title: Keep identifiers compact
sizing.description: The chip grows with its content. Prefer a short brand name and a distinguishing account suffix.

content.title: Distinguish similar accounts
content.description: Keep the brand name recognizable. Include the account suffix when more than one account shares the same brand.

inContext.title: Show the account in use
inContext.description: The surrounding composition explains the chip’s role.

doDont.title: Keep identity recognizable and useful
doDont.description: Match the identity, distinguish accounts, and keep the chip focused on identification.
blocks: Avoid identical labels for different accounts.
Use an avatar or monogram for the brand named in the label.
A different brand cue creates uncertainty about the account.
Keep the brand and the distinguishing suffix.
Long descriptions consume space needed by surrounding content.
Use nearby content for the transaction status.
Do not replace identity with status
A status label no longer tells people which account is involved.

sources.title: Use the public identity slot
sources.description: The guide uses the published Brand Chip component with a consumer-supplied public Avatar.
blocks: Declared, installed, and registry jfs-components versions are 0.1.60. Figma exposes a Label property and an Avatar at S size. The monogram here is supplied through the public avatarSlot; it is not an automatic image-error fallback. The package supports an optional action but exposes no selected or disabled state. Its label is one line by default; use short identifiers in constrained hosts.
